core_obligations: Reduce to a global section: work locally on the integral target, write the meromorphic section as a quotient of two global sections, and note that the two required identities for those sections imply the statement by additivity of divisors (proof lines 4501-4515).

Apply the prepared geometric identity: for a global section, the cycle identity comparing the zero scheme of the pulled back section with the sum over the components of the divisors of the restricted sections gives one side of the equation (proof lines 4516-4522).

Identify the other side: the flat pullback of the divisor of the section is the flat pullback of a cycle class, hence the class of the inverse image of the zero scheme, which is the zero scheme of the pulled back section, giving the equality (proof lines 4523-4529).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to global sections and use additivity (proof lines 4501-4515).
Apply the prepared identity for a global section (proof lines 4516-4522).
Identify the pulled back divisor with the class of the inverse image (proof lines 4523-4529).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the flat pullback of the divisor of a nonzero meromorphic section of an invertible sheaf as the sum over the irreducible components of the divisors of the restricted sections, weighted by the multiplicities (statement lines 4483-4499, tag 02SS-adjacent). The proof reduces to global sections using additivity of divisors, applies the prepared identity comparing the zero scheme of the pulled back section with the sum of the restricted divisors, and identifies the flat pullback of the divisor with the class of the inverse image via the cycle class of a divisor and flat pullback of coherent sheaves. The reduction and the identification are the substance, so the claim is H2.
